The journey

Leave your room, then head north in PALLET TOWN to meet OAK. Choose a starter in his lab. Visit VIRIDIAN MART and return OAK's parcel to receive your POKéDEX and balls. Train in the grass, heal at any POKéMON CENTER, and challenge BROCK in PEWTER.

Continue through MT. MOON to CERULEAN. Help BILL on ROUTE 25 for the S.S. TICKET. The S.S. ANNE captain grants CUT. CELADON's mansion grants TEA for SAFFRON. Defeat GIOVANNI in the ROCKET HIDEOUT for the SILPH SCOPE, then climb POKéMON TOWER for the POKé FLUTE. Find SURF in the SAFARI ZONE's secret house, return GOLD TEETH to the WARDEN for STRENGTH, and find the SECRET KEY in the POKéMON MANSION. Clear SILPH CO., collect all eight badges, then challenge the ELITE FOUR and BLUE.

Party, catching, and saving

Weaken wild POKéMON before throwing a ball from ITEM. Status conditions help. You can carry six; further catches go to the PC. Interact with computers in POKéMON CENTERS to exchange your party and box. Party selection lets you switch your lead or view stats. ITEM handles potions, revival, evolution stones, fishing, and TMs. Trade evolutions use LINK STONE, available at marts.

Save from the top bar or the START menu. Progress is also saved after battles and map transitions. Continue loads that save. The manual's backup controls download or import a JSON save; keep a backup if you move or rename this file. Demo never changes your saved adventure.

Included content and differences

222 original map layouts, all 151 species, all 165 move definitions, original encounter tables and trainer parties, eight gyms, the Elite Four, and legendary encounters. The engine, dialogue sequencing, progression scripts, and sound playback are recreated. NPC movement, some puzzles and scripted scenes, exact move effects, trading, and link battles differ from the original. Original map tiles, fonts, Pokémon sprites, and melody data are used; sound effects and cries are approximations. No speech or scan lines.

Source assets and reference data: pret/pokered. Pokémon belongs to Nintendo, Game Freak, and Creatures. Unofficial recreation, unaffiliated with the original publishers.
